messages:
jonah: Quick follow-up to the adaptive-rate RFC — proposing an AdmissionController v2 interface to support short-term predictive reserves + decaying abuse scores. Wanted to put the tradeoffs here before I open an RFC PR.

jonah: Problem: noisy bursty tenants + a few bad actors cause tail latency spikes when the router tries to fill GPUs. Current token-lease model is brittle for short spikes.

jonah: Proposal sketch: add a small per-tenant predictive_reserve bucket that can be consumed ahead of lease grants for latency-sensitive endpoints. The reserve refills by a learned slope, and consumption increments an abuse_score that decays over time (half-life tunable).

jonah: Example config fields:
```
AdmissionControllerConfig {
  predictive_reserve_tokens: 200,
  reserve_refill_slope: 10, // tokens/sec baseline
  abuse_half_life_secs: 300,
  abuse_penalty_multiplier: 2.5, // multiplies admission backoff
  endpoint_shapes: {"chat_v1": "latency_budget_percentile=95,budget_ms=200"}
}
```

sam: I like the predictive reserve concept. Two immediate questions: how do we prevent long-running jobs from gaming the reserve (draining it and then running slow)? and who owns the learning of refill_slope? router or admission controller?

jonah: Good q. For long-running jobs we bind reserves to a short TTL and make long-running allocations count against the normal lease pool immediately. Reserve only for request/response short RPCs. Refill slope learned by a control plane service that observes per-tenant request arrival rates and signals a suggested slope; admission controller enforces with local caps.

maria: Think about abuse score signal sources: infra should feed failed auths, high rejection rates, and token churn. Also include sample-based evals (response quality anomalies) as inputs. Decay should be exponential so we naturally forgive.

tanvi: Tradeoff: predictive reserve lowers p50/p90 latency at the cost of slightly higher p99 for other tenants when reserves are hit. We need telemetry: reserve_hit_rate, reserve_eviction_count, reserve_steal_conflicts, and per-tenant fairness_delta.

kevin: Interface boundary thoughts — AdmissionController should expose decision reasons for the router (e.g., "ALLOW_RESERVE", "DENY_ABUSE", "FALLBACK_LEASE"). Router uses that to pick model variant or region. Keep policy evaluation synchronous but cache decisions for ~1s to avoid chattiness.

sam: How about a sliding window percentiles module to set endpoint_shapes automatically? If we can set budget_ms from observed p95 latencies we can auto-tune without ops.

jonah: Yes — auto-shaping is optional. But I'd like to keep a manual override per endpoint. Auto-tuner runs in control plane, suggests shapes; engineers can lock them.

maria: Security note: expose audit logs for every reserve grant/consume with request_id and decision_reason. We must ensure these logs are scrubbed of PII and rotated per retention policy.

tanvi: Simulation ask: can we run the new reserve model against the synthetic tenant load in the chaos harness? I can add a config that toggles reserve parameters and measure fairness_delta and tail-latency regressions.

jonah: That would be great — please add two modes: conservative and aggressive. Conservative: low reserve, longer half-life; aggressive: larger reserve, shorter half-life.

ops-bot: deploy-check: no changes detected to prod config. Remember to file RFC PR and link the simulation artifacts.

kevin: One more operational corner: when clusters are under capacity pressure, reserve grants should be disabled globally. Have admission controller check a cluster_capacity_flag and return DENY_RESERVE. Router will then use standard lease path.

sam: +1. Also we should ensure metrics have tenant annotations so SRE can set alerting on reserve abuse patterns.

jonah: Thanks all — I'll draft the RFC with API surface, sample config, simulation plan, and a migration path (feature flag, canary rollout, metrics). Will ping for reviews once PR is up. :wave:
